attempts.label: DANDI:000128
attempts.paper_title: Cortical preparatory activity: representation of movement or first cog in a dynamical machine?
attempts.entry_title: Preparatory and peri-movement tuning in motor and premotor cortex (Churchland et al. 2010)
attempts.summary: Of the findings that could be tested in this one array session, most hold up, but the paper's central claim of only weak agreement between preparatory and movement-period tuning did not reproduce. In the dataset the mean tuning correlation was 0.051 (Pearson) and 0.072 (Spearman), against 0.13 and 0.11 in the paper, with no test significant. Only 17 neurons passed the selection, and the paper's unit and trial selection is not recorded. The preparatory space capturing preparatory tuning best, the time course of the correlation, the controls and the model simulations all reproduced, but dimensionality results did not (best performance at 14 dimensions with no decline, and 15 to 18 components for preparatory activity against 7 to 10). Speed-task, single-electrode and EMG findings could not be tested because that data is not in the dandiset, and the anterior-posterior findings lacked unit locations.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Churchland, Cunningham, Kaufman, Ryu and Shenoy (2010) on dandiset 000128 (MC_Maze), which holds the J-array session of monkey Jenkins on the maze task, recorded with two Utah arrays. It tests the correlation between preparatory and peri-movement tuning, its time course, the dimensionality of preparatory activity, the performance and stability of preferred directions in the peri-movement, kinematic and task spaces, and the paper's oscillator model. The speed task, the single-electrode recordings and EMG are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Churchland et al. (2010) from dandiset 000128

outcomes.notes: The dataset has 108 conditions (36 mazes in 3 versions). The unit count is 182 (137 held in, 45 held out), outside 146 plus or minus 14.6, so the three counts do not all match under any reading. Reading (a), all successful trials, gives 2869 with the 574 test-file segments, outside the tolerance, and 2295 counting the train file alone (the trials with condition labels), within it; every unit is observed on every train trial. The test file has its own clock and no delay or success column, so whether its trials belong to (a) cannot be settled from the file. Under reading (b) M1 keeps 1786 trials with T2, outside the tolerance. The 137 held-in units (a Neural Latents Benchmark split) and the 1967 trials with delay > 400 ms are printed but are not readings and decide nothing. The answer of 2026-10-22 to the M1 question removed T1's count (1452) from reading (b); the outcome is unchanged.
deviations: Nothing in the dataset says which units or trials the paper used, or whether this session (2009-09-25) is the one the paper analysed.

outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds only the array session of monkey Jenkins. No speed-task data (monkeys A and B) and no single-electrode maze recordings are in it, and the paper names no other archive for them.
Needs the speed task, which is not in the dandiset.
Needs the speed task, which is not in the dandiset.

Under T2 with S1, 1 of 17 neurons has r of 0.72 or more (0.765) and 94.1% have r below 0.72, so the claim holds. The first part rests on that one neuron (unit 1581); the next largest r is 0.457. The answers of 2026-10-22 set aside T1 and S2. The earlier record was blocked (methods_underspecified) because T1 with S1 gave no neuron at 0.72 and S2 selected no neuron; with T2 and S1 fixed, the claim is reproduced. The notebook no longer prints T1 or S2 values.

Under T2 with S1, 17 neurons, the mean Pearson r is 0.051 and the mean Spearman r 0.072, outside 0.13 plus or minus 0.013 and 0.11 plus or minus 0.011, and no test gives p below 0.05 (P1 0.47, P2 0.42, P3 0.61). Both means are positive; the Pearson mean is below half the paper's (0.065) and the Spearman mean is 65% of the paper's. Per-neuron r runs from -0.355 to 0.765 (SD 0.283); with 17 neurons the tests have little power. The answers of 2026-10-22 set aside T1 and S2; the earlier record gave T1 with S1 (recorded then as measured) and T2 with S1, and S2 gave no neuron; the notebook no longer prints T1 or S2 values. The measured values are now those of T2, and the outcome is unchanged.
deviations: The dataset has 182 units, not the paper's 146, and the paper's unit selection is not recorded; the selected neurons may differ from the paper's.

outcomes.notes: The single-electrode datasets of monkeys A, B and J are not in the dandiset.

J-array only. Under T2 with S1 the dip statistic is 0.071 (p 0.683), so U1 holds, and 16 of 17 neurons have |r| below 0.5, so U2 holds. No neuron has |r| of 0.8 or more; median r 0.013. With 17 neurons the dip test has little power, so U1 is weak evidence. The panel B part of the statement (monkey B) cannot be tested. The answers of 2026-10-22 removed the T1 and S2 readings, which had given the same outcome (T1) or no neuron (S2); the outcome is unchanged.

Under T2 with S1 (17 neurons), the mean correlation is 0.737 (A1) and 0.759 (A2) at -400 ms, 0.608 at -200 ms and 0.012 at movement onset, where no test is significant (smallest p 0.854). 82.1% (A1) and 79.8% (A2) of the drop from -400 ms to onset comes after -200 ms. The answers of 2026-10-22 removed the T1 and S2 readings, which had given the same outcome (T1) or no neuron (S2); the outcome is unchanged.
deviations: Under A2 the criterion's linear joining was implemented as a straight line between the last go-locked value and the first movement-locked one where they leave a gap, and a linear fade from one to the other where they overlap, with each condition's go cue placed at its mean reaction time before onset. A1 and A2 differ only before -300 ms and give the same outcome.

outcomes.notes: Under T2 with S1 (17 neurons), the strongest-minus-weakest separation is 0.220 (reading a) and 0.346 (reading b) of the maximum rate in the preparatory epoch, and 0.053 and 0.095 at movement onset, ratios 0.240 and 0.274. R1 holds under both; R2 holds under (a) and not under (b). The preparatory separation is positive by construction, as the conditions are ranked on the same preparatory rates. The answer of 2026-10-22 says the paper does not fix the maximum, and the criterion now names readings (a) and (b), the two already run, so the method is unchanged. The answers on M1 and M6 removed T1 and S2; the outcome is unchanged.

Under T2 with S1 (83 neurons) the peri-movement space is best in 24 of 24 combinations of W, D, V and G under K1 and under K2. Its best is 0.518 at k = 14 (K1) and 0.505 at k = 12 (K2), against 0.424 and 0.417 for the best kinematic space and 0.412 for the kitchen-sink space (G1). The best k is the upper end of each range, an edge value and not a peak. The answers of 2026-10-22 set aside T1 and S2. The earlier record was blocked (methods_underspecified) because under T1 with S1 the peri-movement space fell below the kinematic and kitchen-sink spaces (values no longer printed); with T2 fixed, the claim is reproduced.
deviations: J-array only; EMG is not recorded for it.
Acceleration is the time derivative of the dataset's hand velocity.
V1 ("each component's maximum absolute value") was run as the magnitudes (V1a) and as the signed component at its largest magnitude (V1b); they do not change the outcome.

outcomes.notes: The 3-D endpoints + max speed space (0.168) is below the 3-D peri-movement space (0.271). Under T2 with S1 the peri-movement space wins 21 of 22 comparisons (K1) and 19 of 20 (K2) in every combination of W, D, V and G, so L1 and L2 hold. The comparison lost is the 2-D initial-velocity space (0.238 against 0.223). At k = 1 the peri-movement space beats the kinematic spaces by 0.002 to 0.004 only. The answers of 2026-10-22 set aside T1 and S2. The earlier record was blocked (methods_underspecified) because T1 failed L1 and L2 and T2 with S2 failed L1 in some combinations; with T2 and S1 fixed, the claim is reproduced.

Under T2 with S1 (83 neurons) performance rises from 0.140 at k = 1 to 0.518 at k = 14, so it improves with dimensionality, but the best k is 14, above 10, and performance does not decline at k = 14. Two of the criterion's three conditions fail, and the part of the statement they test (a peak in a middle range and a decline beyond about 10 dimensions) is not found. The answers of 2026-10-22 set aside T1 and S2. The earlier record was blocked (methods_underspecified) because under T1 the claim held (values no longer printed); with T2 fixed, it is not reproduced.

Under T2, 90% of the variance of the preparatory condition-mean matrix needs 15 components with the 83 neurons of N1 (S1) and 18 with all 182 units (N2). Neither is within 7 to 11. The supplement defines the matrix as the claims file does ("T was c×n with each row containing the mean preparatory activity for every neuron"), from "all neurons", which is reading N2 (18), and says "7-10 dimensions were required"; the main text says "at least 7-10 dimensions", which 15 and 18 would meet. Whether the claim is a range or a lower bound is asked in questions/000128.yaml. The condition means average 10 to 22 trials per condition (median 17), and their noise may add components; the claims file does not fix how the paper handled this. The answers of 2026-10-22 set aside T1 (recorded earlier as measured) and S2; the measured value is now 15 and the outcome is unchanged.
Needs monkeys A, B and J (single electrodes) and EMG, none of which is in the dandiset.

Under T2 with S1 the shuffled space (mean of 10 shuffles) is below the unshuffled one at every k, so H1 holds, and its best, 0.227 (0.208 to 0.244 over shuffles), is below the best kinematic space in every variant (0.421 or more under K1, 0.414 or more under K2), so H2 holds. The answers of 2026-10-22 set aside T1 and S2. The earlier record was blocked (methods_underspecified) because under T1 the unshuffled space fell below zero at k of 10 or more while the shuffled one stayed positive, so H1 failed; with T2 fixed, the claim is reproduced.
deviations: J-array only; the paper averages over datasets.

outcomes.notes: Reading J2, the J-array ratio. Under T2 with S1, performance at the best k with the window starting at onset is 0.959 (K1) and 0.957 (K2) of that with the window starting at -150 ms, within 0.97 plus or minus 0.097. The 94% of monkeys A and B and the single-electrode J value (J1) cannot be tested. Both best k values are the upper end of their range. The answers of 2026-10-22 set aside T1 and S2, which had all been within tolerance (T1 was recorded earlier as measured); the measured value is now 0.959 and the outcome is unchanged.

The electrodes table has no coordinates, so no anterior-posterior location. The criterion's fallback, the array, is not usable either, as every unit's electrode reference points into the 96 PMd rows, so by the file all units are in PMd. The unit ids' leading digit (1 for 92 units, 2 for 90) looks like an array number, but nothing in the dataset documents it or which array is which. As a variant that decides nothing, regressing tuning correlation on that digit gives r of magnitude 0.432 (T2 with S1, 17 neurons, p 0.084), not significant. The electrode groups are described as one array in M1 and one in PMd, but no unit column other than the electrode reference maps a unit to a group. The answers of 2026-10-22 removed the T1 variant; the block is unchanged.
Needs each unit's AP location or at least its array; see ap-location-no-effect-on-correlation. Not run.

Under T2 with S1 the peri-movement space has the higher mean PD consistency in all 11 comparisons (0.752 against 0.548 for endpoints + max speed, 0.649 and 0.648 against 0.495 and 0.466 for segment directions G1 and G2, and 0.197 to 0.319 against 0.166 to 0.230 for the kinematic spaces at their best k, which is the upper end of the range). The answers of 2026-10-22 removed the T1 and S2 readings, which had given the same outcome; the outcome is unchanged. Removing them changed the random draws, so the values differ slightly from the earlier record.

Over 1000 draws of 25 initial states, the correlation has medians -0.041 to 0.019, and the central 95% ranges have lower bounds of -0.430 to -0.385 and upper bounds of 0.350 to 0.428 under the eight readings; 0.08 lies inside all of them. The second part of the statement (a given preparatory rate leading to opposing patterns) is not tested by the criterion.
Under all eight readings the smallest R squared and leave-one-out performance over 100 draws are 1.0 to the printed precision.

findings.statement: Every unit's electrode reference in the units table points into the first 96 rows of the electrodes table, which are labelled PMd, so by the file all 182 units are in PMd. The dataset describes two arrays, in M1 and PMd. The reference equals the unit id's channel digits minus one, which suggests the array offset was dropped in conversion.

The electrodes have no coordinates (x, y and z are NaN), and the leading digit of the unit ids (1 or 2), which may be the array, is not documented. No unit can be placed on the anterior-posterior axis or on an array.
The dataset holds 182 units where the paper reports 146 isolations for the J-array dataset, and does not record which units or trials the paper used, or that this session is the paper's.

574 of the session's successful trials are in the test file as 0.7 s segments around movement onset, without condition labels or behaviour and with only the 137 held-in units, so they cannot enter a condition-mean analysis. None duplicates a train trial. The test file has a clock of its own (segment times restart at 0) and no delay or success column, and the train file's trial ids are contiguous, so the files do not record which session trials the packaging dropped.
14 trials have a negative delay (as low as -3 ms), where the go cue precedes the recorded target onset.
